**Strategic Architecture — Modulated Sovereign-Cloud Integration & Corridor-Certification Platform**  
*“One Global Data-Integrity Backbone; Certified Regional Sovereignty-Visibility-Commitment Profiles”*

The failure mode in rapid twelve-market rollout is treating **data-sovereignty divergence (local-control celebration vs. global-parity preservation vs. hybrid-fractured procurement)**, **procurement-trust divergence (government-trust / vendor-trust / foreign-vendor preference)**, **feature-parity divergence (zero-delay expectation vs. regional-release lag)**, **price-interpretation divergence (cost-neutral migration vs. extraction fear)**, **government-access divergence (transparent legal-boundary vs. surveillance-risk)**, **cross-border remote-worker data divergence (diaspora clusters transmitting contradictory sovereignty norms)**, **hidden Western-HQ architecture dependency (metadata, analytics, encryption-key management, disaster-recovery, or collaboration-layer still routing through unaudited US/EU-West-Coast node)**, **partner-legal maturity asymmetry (local data-protection counsel / cloud-auditor / procurement board unprepared for localized liability)**, and **organizational-trust architecture divergence (enterprise-procurement hierarchy-trust vs. autonomous-customer-output trust vs. partner-vendor intermediary trust)** as “regulatory localization”: copying the mature-region (EU GDPR-style direct-residency / unified global-cloud-template / universal feature-parity API / 90-day universal migration contract) model into all twelve country markets without **process-integrated corridor-certification and cultural-interaction licensing**; signing rapid-deployment contracts that hide upstream global-process dependencies (e.g., a “São Paulo sovereign cloud” still routing analytics, encryption-key escrow, and collaboration metadata through an unaudited Western-HQ node with hidden single-region dependency); allowing regional leadership to interpret every customer data-boundary request, procurement-negotiation reserve, or feature-parity demand as global-margin extraction; and delaying core **data-ontology specification / partner-legal correlation / procurement-culture audit / feature-parity verification / government-access protocol verification / remote-diaspora divergence audit** until a **2026 sovereign-cloud backlash crisis, government-access scandal, cross-border contamination spill (C-LOC customer posting about C-GLOB “surveillance cloud” spreading via LinkedIn / procurement networks to enterprise buyers in twelve markets within hours), hidden-Western-node exposure, feature-parity collapse, price-boycott escalation, customer-contract lockout (SLA breach due to uncovered residency gap), organizational-procurement trust collapse, or data-protection audit (local-regulator suspension)** forces emergency withdrawal—resulting in **corridor-specification divergence** (hidden primary-source Western-cloud dependency behind “localized” Brazil / Mexico / Colombia / Eastern-Europe data-residency policy), **unverified sovereignty-claims** (“regional cloud” that leaks metadata back to global HQ), **regulatory/enforcement action** (data-protection board suspension; enterprise-procurement boycott; contract-breach grievance), **counterparty and partner-legal abandonment and reputation-spoilage**, or **permanent competitive loss to locally certified regional vendors (local sovereign-cloud providers with verified residency contracts)**.

The correct model is a **modulated global sovereign-cloud platform**: a standardized global **data-integrity backbone** (non-negotiable ethical-data taxonomy for Tier **S—Systemic-Strategic** / core residency-ontology, feature-parity rules, government-access protocol, anti-fragmentation registry, crisis-firewall, qualification-registry, partner-legal pipeline, data-protection architecture, diaspora-monitor backbone, collaboration-tool tracking, analytics-boundary architecture / Tier **C—Critical-Functional** / regional pilot-corridor nodes, legal-submission nodes, client-contract nodes, feature-parity nodes, price-stability nodes, remote-diaspora nodes, organizational-trust nodes / Tier **R—Replaceable-Standard** / migration-template assets, notification-copy files, feature-parity-checklist packaging, sovereignty-dialogue materials, data-exit-notification copy, seasonal-pilot packaging) with defined jurisdiction-residency, corridor-certification baseline, and legal/community/stakeholder requirements; a **separated commitment-component registry** tracking every regional corridor agreement as **Migration Investment (corridor-qualification / pilot-corridor correlation / partner-legal-certification / feature-parity audit / government-access audit / procurement-culture audit / remote-diaspora audit)** + **Local Trust Reservation (data-protection reserve / feature-parity reserve / price-stability reserve / government-access reserve / procurement-conflict reserve / diaspora-monitor reserve)** + **Group Cloud Subscription (Base unified sovereign-delivery + Swing/Protection for regional continuity/crisis-protection)** + **Transition Window / Pilot Quarter (quarters)**; a **dual-corridor verification rule**—a “qualified corridor” means full residency-correlation, partner-legal verification, feature-parity verification, procurement-trust verification, language-native verification, symbolic-precision correlation, organizational-trust audit, diaspora-divergence audit, client-contract isolation verification, hidden upstream global-cloud/dependency mapping completed—not a translated compliance manual with localized imagery; a **fragmentation firewall** preventing unqualified (**B0/B1**) corridor claims, “paper dual-compliance” status (e.g., a “Colombia sovereign cloud” still routing analytics and encryption management through an unaudited Western-HQ node with hidden single-region dependencies), or hidden Western-core architecture dependencies; **interaction geo-traceability mandate**—every data-residency event, migration-release event, feature-verification interval, procurement-dialogue signal, client-contract amendment, and symbolic-adaptation mapped to jurisdiction cluster with upstream global-cloud node and legal-dependency flagged; and a **global crisis-escalation protocol** for government-access scandal, feature-parity collapse, price-boycott escalation, cross-border contamination, partner-legal collapse, hidden-cloud-node breach, client-contract lockout, procurement-trust escalation, organizational-access breach, or data-protection audit.

### 2. The Three Certified Regional Sovereignty Profiles

**Profile C-LOC — Local-Sovereignty Affirmative / High Government-Trust / Procurement Celebrates / Feature-Parity Confident / Low Foreign-Vendor Preference Risk**
*Sovereignty-Procurement Covenant:* This cluster demands **full residency-verification** (customer data physically and legally resident in national/regional cloud; encryption keys managed within jurisdiction; government-access protocols are transparent, legally bounded, and auditable—not hidden), **procurement-celebration verification** (enterprise buyers and regulators interpret localization as vendor legitimacy; they do not fear government overreach but demand proof that access is rule-bound), **feature-parity confidence verification** (customers expect zero feature loss versus legacy global architecture; any regional-release lag must be pre-certified with timeline, not discovered post-migration), **foreign-vendor independence verification** (trust is placed in local regulatory framework more than in vendor’s global brand; the vendor must prove it is not “hiding” data elsewhere), **language-sovereignty verification** (local legal terms—“residency,” “key-escrow,” “government-access log,” “data-protection audit”—not generic “cloud security” translation), and **remote-diaspora divergence audit** (cross-border remote-worker clusters in this cluster must not import global-integration expectations that conflict with local sovereignty rules).

- **Migration / Certification Boundary:** 18-month regulatory-aligned milestone-gated B2; local-residency must cover verified local data-protection-counsel audit and government-access-board verification; feature-parity certified with client-procurement board; hidden-global-node dependency mapped and eliminated; pilot-cohort retention/churn-risk tracking completed; government-access transparency portal live.
- **Counterparty / Stakeholder-Trust Covenant:** Government-trust and local-sovereignty belief dominate; customer and procurement trust requires **verified elimination of hidden global-node dependencies (not just “regional instance” marketing), transparent government-access logs with independent audit board, direct local-customer-success access without global-queue gatekeeping, visible commitment to feature-parity timeline, and zero “shadow backup” to Western HQ**; economic/access terms must be transparent in local language with regulatory-counsel disclosure.
- **Channel / Governance Profile:** Local-residency core + government-access-transparency automation + feature-parity certification + encryption-key-sovereignty verification + procurement-celebration dialogue board + local regulatory-counsel audit + remote-diaspora isolation rules; rapid pure-global-parity rollout without verified residency pipeline is B0/B1 only.
- **Dependency Exposure Label:** Hidden-Western-HQ-Cloud Dependency (metadata, analytics, or disaster-recovery routing through unaudited US/EU node); Feature-Parity Over-Confidence (promising full parity before certification); Procurement-Reversal Risk (government-access scandal destroying celebration); Cross-Border Contamination (C-GLOB diaspora criticizing “surveillance” in internal procurement networks).
- **Stakeholder-Communication Covenant:** Residency-rules, government-access-covenant, feature-parity-certification timeline, hidden-node-elimination proof, procurement-dialogue rules, remote-worker sovereignty rules, crisis-escalation pathway, and legal/access disclosure published to local regulators, procurement boards, and customer-success monitors.
- **Trust-Economics:** Migration Investment = local-cloud build + government-access audit pipeline + feature-parity verification + regulatory-counsel audit + procurement-dialogue board + remote-diaspora reserve; Local Trust Reservation = data-protection reserve / feature-parity reserve / government-access reserve / procurement-conflict reserve / cross-contamination reserve; Group Subscription = Base verified sovereign-delivery + Swing for government-access crisis-protection and feature-parity defense; Transition Window = 4-quarter pilot-to-certification cycle (single-division pilot → cluster B2).

**Profile C-GLOB — Global-Integration Preference / Low Government-Trust / High Foreign-Vendor Trust / Procurement Fears Fragmentation / Price/Feature Sensitive / High Churn Risk**
*Sovereignty-Procurement Covenant:* This cluster demands **global-parity preservation verification** (any localization must not reduce feature set, increase latency for global workflows, or create data-isolation barriers that break cross-border collaboration; customers prefer the legacy single-region architecture’s consistency), **foreign-vendor loyalty protection** (procurement trusts the vendor’s global brand and engineering capacity more than local government infrastructure; localization is interpreted as either vendor weakness, cost-shifting to customer, or government-coercion risk), **price-stability verification** (customers fear localization will trigger price increases, dual-billing, or subscription-tier fragmentation; economic terms must be locked and transparent), **government-access risk mitigation** (procurement fears that local clouds increase exposure to government surveillance, data seizure, or regulatory instability; vendor must prove independence and legal-defense capacity), **feature-delay crisis-prevention** (any regional-release lag is interpreted as vendor abandonment of global product excellence), **organizational-trust preservation** (enterprise procurement boards invested in global vendor relationships must see that localization enhances—not erodes—vendor credibility), and **opt-in/phased migration covenant** (mandatory universal migration is culturally toxic; customers demand choice, exit rights, and phased timelines).

- **Certification Boundary:** Staged partner-build across procurement, client-contract, and feature-parity nodes; B2 requires verified global-parity preservation, price-lock subscription audit, government-access-risk mitigation board clearance, feature-delay zero-tolerance verification, organizational-trust board clearance, and opt-in migration architecture.
- **Counterparty / Stakeholder-Trust Covenant:** Foreign-vendor loyalty and global-integration belief dominate; customer and procurement trust requires **verified preservation of feature-parity (no hidden regional degradation), transparent price-lock (no hidden localization surcharge), direct global-customer-success continuity (no regional-queue isolation), visible vendor independence from government overreach, explicit data-repatriation/exit rights, and zero mandatory-migration coercion**; economic/access terms must preserve global contract investment.
- **Channel / Governance Profile:** Global-parity-preservation core + opt-in local-residency module (never mandatory without parity proof) + price-stability covenant + government-access-risk mitigation architecture + feature-parity defense board + foreign-vendor loyalty dialogue board + organizational-trust audit + legal-opt-in/repatriation design; rapid universal localization rollout without verified parity pipeline is B0/B1 only and triggers crisis.
- **Dependency Exposure Label:** Hidden-Global-Node Dependency (if vendor claims localization but keeps primary processing global—this destroys C-GLOB trust); Feature-Parity Collapse (regional cloud lacks capabilities); Price-Extraction Backlash; Government-Surveillance Fear Spill; Enterprise-Churn Cascade to global competitors.
- **Stakeholder-Communication Covenant:** Opt-in migration rules, global-parity-preservation covenant, price-lock architecture, government-access-independence proof, feature-parity defense timeline, foreign-vendor loyalty transparency, crisis-escalation pathway, and legal/repatriation disclosure in procurement-trusted terminology.
- **Trust-Economics:** Migration Investment = global-parity preservation pipeline + price-lock architecture + government-access-risk board + feature-parity verification + organizational-trust board + opt-in/repatriation legal design + foreign-vendor loyalty reserve; Local Trust Reservation = feature-parity reserve / price-stability reserve / government-access-risk reserve / procurement-conflict reserve / churn-defense reserve; Group Subscription = Base global-integrity verified delivery + Swing for parity-collapse crisis-protection and enterprise-continuity defense; Transition Window = 2–3 quarter staged procurement/dialogue-build cycle (no universal launch).

**Profile C-FRAC — Hybrid-Fractured / Regulatory Emerging / Mixed Procurement / Cross-Border Data Contamination Critical / Legal-Maturity Asymmetric / Diaspora-Remote Critical**
*Sovereignty-Procurement Covenant:* This cluster is the highest-risk integration node. It demands **hybrid-fracture verification** (young/regional champions demand local residency and government-access transparency; global/procurement HQ demands feature-parity and foreign-vendor loyalty; remote-worker and diaspora clusters transmit contradictory sovereignty norms across borders within hours; labor/data-protection law exists but enforcement, collective agreement, and cloud-auditor capacity are uneven), **dual-corridor coexistence verification** (the architecture must explicitly separate C-LOC-style residency nodes and C-GLOB-style global-parity nodes within the same market/contract without organizational-conflict or hidden-hierarchy—verified by procurement-dialogue board—not “one policy for all”), **cross-border contamination firewall** (remote-worker clusters, diaspora consultants, or multi-national procurement teams in São Paulo / Mexico City / Bogotá / Singapore / Berlin must not import sovereignty norms from one cluster into another, spreading criticism via internal Slack, LinkedIn, or procurement networks), **client-contract isolation verification** (enterprise contracts in this cluster are often split—some clients require local-residency SLAs, others require global-parity SLAs; the vendor must verify contract isolation, not apply a blended ambiguous standard), **legal-maturity asymmetry acknowledgment** (local data-protection counsel may be unprepared to audit encryption-key management or government-access protocols; vendor must co-build audit capacity, not assume readiness), **feature-parity fracture management** (regional feature releases may lag; the vendor must pre-certify which features are globally synchronized and which are regionally deferred, avoiding hidden disappointment), and **crisis-readiness for government-access and feature-delay simultaneous shock** (this cluster is most vulnerable to compound crisis: a local government-access request combined with a feature-parity complaint can trigger rapid cross-border contamination).

- **Certification Boundary:** Milestone-gated B2 with hybrid-architecture audit; requires verified dual-corridor separation, cross-border contamination firewall test, client-contract isolation audit, remote-diaspora divergence audit, feature-parity fracture disclosure, government-access protocol verification, local legal-capacity co-build, and organizational-trust board clearance.
- **Counterparty / Stakeholder-Trust Covenant:** Mixed procurement-trust and organizational-access culture dominate; stakeholder trust requires **verified separation of local-residency and global-parity nodes within same contract, transparent disclosure of feature-parity fractures (not hidden post-sale), explicit remote-worker/data-boundary rules, direct access to both local-regulatory and global-product leadership, visible anti-contamination firewall (internal/external social monitoring), zero blended-ambiguous contract language, and co-built local-legal audit capacity**; economic/access terms must accommodate split procurement boards.
- **Channel / Governance Profile:** Hybrid-fractured core + dual-track migration option (residency-track vs. parity-track) + feature-parity fracture disclosure + cross-border contamination firewall + client-contract isolation architecture + remote-diaspora rules + government-access protocol + local-legal co-build; rapid universal single-track rollout is B0/B1 and triggers compound crisis.

### 2. The Three Certified Regional Sovereignty Profiles

**Profile C-LOC — Local-Sovereignty Affirmative / High Government-Trust / Procurement Celebrates / Feature-Parity Confident / Low Foreign-Vendor Preference Risk**
*Sovereignty-Procurement Covenant:* This cluster demands **full residency-verification** (customer data physically and legally resident in national/regional cloud; encryption keys managed within jurisdiction; government-access protocols are transparent, legally bounded, and auditable—not hidden), **procurement-celebration verification** (enterprise buyers and regulators interpret localization as vendor legitimacy; they do not fear government overreach but demand proof that access is rule-bound), **feature-parity confidence verification** (customers expect zero feature loss versus legacy global architecture; any regional-release lag must be pre-certified with timeline, not discovered post-migration), **foreign-vendor independence verification** (trust is placed in local regulatory framework more than in vendor’s global brand; the vendor must prove it is not “hiding” data elsewhere), **language-sovereignty verification** (local legal terms—“residency,” “key-escrow,” “government-access log,” “data-protection audit”—not generic “cloud security” translation), and **remote-diaspora divergence audit** (cross-border remote-worker clusters in this cluster must not import global-integration expectations that conflict with local sovereignty rules).

- **Migration / Certification Boundary:** 18-month regulatory-aligned milestone-gated B2; local-residency must cover verified local data-protection-counsel audit and government-access-board verification; feature-parity certified with client-procurement board; hidden-global-node dependency mapped and eliminated; pilot-cohort retention/churn-risk tracking completed; government-access transparency portal live.
- **Counterparty / Stakeholder-Trust Covenant:** Government-trust and local-sovereignty belief dominate; customer and procurement trust requires **verified elimination of hidden global-node dependencies (not just “regional instance” marketing), transparent government-access logs with independent audit board, direct local-customer-success access without global-queue gatekeeping, visible commitment to feature-parity timeline, and zero “shadow backup” to Western HQ**; economic/access terms must be transparent in local language with regulatory-counsel disclosure.
- **Channel / Governance Profile:** Local-residency core + government-access-transparency automation + feature-parity certification + encryption-key-sovereignty verification + procurement-celebration dialogue board + local regulatory-counsel audit + remote-diaspora isolation rules; rapid pure-global-parity rollout without verified residency pipeline is B0/B1 only.
- **Dependency Exposure Label:** Hidden-Western-HQ-Cloud Dependency (metadata, analytics, or disaster-recovery routing through unaudited US/EU node); Feature-Parity Over-Confidence (promising full parity before certification); Procurement-Reversal Risk (government-access scandal destroying celebration); Cross-Border Contamination (C-GLOB diaspora criticizing “surveillance” in internal procurement networks).
- **Stakeholder-Communication Covenant:** Residency-rules, government-access-covenant, feature-parity-certification timeline, hidden-node-elimination proof, procurement-dialogue rules, remote-worker sovereignty rules, crisis-escalation pathway, and legal/access disclosure published to local regulators, procurement boards, and customer-success monitors.
- **Trust-Economics:** Migration Investment = local-cloud build + government-access audit pipeline + feature-parity verification + regulatory-counsel audit + procurement-dialogue board + remote-diaspora reserve; Local Trust Reservation = data-protection reserve / feature-parity reserve / government-access reserve / procurement-conflict reserve / cross-contamination reserve; Group Subscription = Base verified sovereign-delivery + Swing for government-access crisis-protection and feature-parity defense; Transition Window = 4-quarter pilot-to-certification cycle (single-division pilot → cluster B2).

**Profile C-GLOB — Global-Integration Preference / Low Government-Trust / High Foreign-Vendor Trust / Procurement Fears Fragmentation / Price/Feature Sensitive / High Churn Risk**
*Sovereignty-Procurement Covenant:* This cluster demands **global-parity preservation verification** (any localization must not reduce feature set, increase latency for global workflows, or create data-isolation barriers that break cross-border collaboration; customers prefer the legacy single-region architecture’s consistency), **foreign-vendor loyalty protection** (procurement trusts the vendor’s global brand and engineering capacity more than local government infrastructure; localization is interpreted as either vendor weakness, cost-shifting to customer, or government-coercion risk), **price-stability verification** (customers fear localization will trigger price increases, dual-billing, or subscription-tier fragmentation; economic terms must be locked and transparent), **government-access risk mitigation** (procurement fears that local clouds increase exposure to government surveillance, data seizure, or regulatory instability; vendor must prove independence and legal-defense capacity), **feature-delay crisis-prevention** (any regional-release lag is interpreted as vendor abandonment of global product excellence), **organizational-trust preservation** (enterprise procurement boards invested in global vendor relationships must see that localization enhances—not erodes—vendor credibility), and **opt-in/phased migration covenant** (mandatory universal migration is culturally toxic; customers demand choice, exit rights, and phased timelines).

- **Certification Boundary:** Staged partner-build across procurement, client-contract, and feature-parity nodes; B2 requires verified global-parity preservation, price-lock subscription audit, government-access-risk mitigation board clearance, feature-delay zero-tolerance verification, organizational-trust board clearance, and opt-in migration architecture.
- **Counterparty / Stakeholder-Trust Covenant:** Foreign-vendor loyalty and global-integration belief dominate; customer and procurement trust requires **verified preservation of feature-parity (no hidden regional degradation), transparent price-lock (no hidden localization surcharge), direct global-customer-success continuity (no regional-queue isolation), visible vendor independence from government overreach, explicit data-repatriation/exit rights, and zero mandatory-migration coercion**; economic/access terms must preserve global contract investment.
- **Channel / Governance Profile:** Global-parity-preservation core + opt-in local-residency module (never mandatory without parity proof) + price-stability covenant + government-access-risk mitigation architecture + feature-parity defense board + foreign-vendor loyalty dialogue board + organizational-trust audit + legal-opt-in/repatriation design; rapid universal localization rollout without verified parity pipeline is B0/B1 only and triggers crisis.
- **Dependency Exposure Label:** Hidden-Global-Node Dependency (if vendor claims localization but keeps primary processing global—this destroys C-GLOB trust); Feature-Parity Collapse (regional cloud lacks capabilities); Price-Extraction Backlash; Government-Surveillance Fear Spill; Enterprise-Churn Cascade to global competitors.
- **Stakeholder-Communication Covenant:** Opt-in migration rules, global-parity-preservation covenant, price-lock architecture, government-access-independence proof, feature-parity defense timeline, foreign-vendor loyalty transparency, crisis-escalation pathway, and legal/repatriation disclosure in procurement-trusted terminology.
- **Trust-Economics:** Migration Investment = global-parity preservation pipeline + price-lock architecture + government-access-risk board + feature-parity verification + organizational-trust board + opt-in/repatriation legal design + foreign-vendor loyalty reserve; Local Trust Reservation = feature-parity reserve / price-stability reserve / government-access-risk reserve / procurement-conflict reserve / churn-defense reserve; Group Subscription = Base global-integrity verified delivery + Swing for parity-collapse crisis-protection and enterprise-continuity defense; Transition Window = 2–3 quarter staged procurement/dialogue-build cycle (no universal launch).

**Profile C-FRAC — Hybrid-Fractured / Regulatory Emerging / Mixed Procurement / Cross-Border Data Contamination Critical / Legal-Maturity Asymmetric / Diaspora-Remote Critical**
*Sovereignty-Procurement Covenant:* This cluster is the highest-risk integration node. It demands **hybrid-fracture verification** (young/regional champions demand local residency and government-access transparency; global/procurement HQ demands feature-parity and foreign-vendor loyalty; remote-worker and diaspora clusters transmit contradictory sovereignty norms across borders within hours; labor/data-protection law exists but enforcement, collective agreement, and cloud-auditor capacity are uneven), **dual-corridor coexistence verification** (the architecture must explicitly separate C-LOC-style residency nodes and C-GLOB-style global-parity nodes within the same market/contract without organizational-conflict or hidden-hierarchy—verified by procurement-dialogue board—not “one policy for all”), **cross-border contamination firewall** (remote-worker clusters, diaspora consultants, or multi-national procurement teams in São Paulo / Mexico City / Bogotá / Singapore / Berlin must not import sovereignty norms from one cluster into another, spreading criticism via internal Slack, LinkedIn, or procurement networks), **client-contract isolation verification** (enterprise contracts in this cluster are often split—some clients require local-residency SLAs, others require global-parity SLAs; the vendor must verify contract isolation, not apply a blended ambiguous standard), **legal-maturity asymmetry acknowledgment** (local data-protection counsel may be unprepared to audit encryption-key management or government-access protocols; vendor must co-build audit capacity, not assume readiness), **feature-parity fracture management** (regional feature releases may lag; the vendor must pre-certify which features are globally synchronized and which are regionally deferred, avoiding hidden disappointment), and **crisis-readiness for government-access and feature-delay simultaneous shock** (this cluster is most vulnerable to compound crisis: a local government-access request combined with a feature-parity complaint can trigger rapid cross-border contamination).

- **Certification Boundary:** Milestone-gated B2 with hybrid-architecture audit; requires verified dual-corridor separation, cross-border contamination firewall test, client-contract isolation audit, remote-diaspora divergence audit, feature-parity fracture disclosure, government-access protocol verification, local legal-capacity co-build, and organizational-trust board clearance.
- **Counterparty / Stakeholder-Trust Covenant:** Mixed procurement-trust and organizational-access culture dominate; stakeholder trust requires **verified separation of local-residency and global-parity nodes within same contract, transparent disclosure of feature-parity fractures (not hidden post-sale), explicit remote-worker/data-boundary rules, direct access to both local-regulatory and global-product leadership, visible anti-contamination firewall (internal/external social monitoring), zero blended-ambiguous contract language, and co-built local-legal audit capacity**; economic/access terms must accommodate split procurement boards.
- **Channel / Governance Profile:** Hybrid-fractured core + dual-track migration option (residency-track vs. parity-track) + feature-parity fracture disclosure + cross-border contamination firewall + client-contract isolation architecture + remote-diaspora rules + government-access protocol + local-legal co-build; rapid universal single-track rollout is B0/B1 and triggers compound crisis.
